docs.title: cheersafe
docs.text:
CHEERSafe: Hurricane loss analysis package for building properties, hazard data, and loss models.

This package provides comprehensive tools for hurricane damage and loss assessment, including building inventory management, load calculations, damage probability analysis, damage ratio calculations, loss estimation, and scenario creation and analysis.

Utilities for data processing, visualization, and statistics

A configuration management class for the CHEERSafe package.

This class provides global configuration settings for the CHEERSafe hurricane damage and loss assessment model. It manages execution behavior, data loading preferences, file paths, and processing parameters used throughout the package.

Attributes:

Name Type Description AUTO_EXECUTE_METHODS bool

Flag to control automatic execution of methods. When True, methods are executed automatically during object initialization. Default is True.

AUTO_LOAD_DATASETS bool

Flag to control automatic loading of datasets. When True, datasets are loaded automatically during object initialization. Default is True.

INPUTS_PATH str

The directory path where input data files are stored. Default is 'Inputs'.

OUTPUTS_PATH str

The directory path where output files will be saved. Default is 'Outputs'.

NUM_OF_ITERATIONS int

The number of iterations to perform in Monte Carlo simulations and other iterative processes. Default is 3000.

NUM_OF_WORKERS int

The number of parallel workers to use for multi-threaded operations. Default is 4.

NUM_OF_WORKERS_SAMPLING int

The number of parallel workers to use specifically for sampling operations. Default is 1.

EXPORT_DETAILED_DAMAGE_RATIOS bool

Flag to enable export of detailed damage ratio breakdowns to CSV files. When True, detailed component-level damage ratios are collected during Monte Carlo simulation and saved as CSV files per (building_type, cindex) combination. This is computationally expensive and disabled by default. Default is False.

docs.text:
process_component_combination(building: Building, ComponentCombination, cIndex: int) -> tuple

Process the component combination for a building with parallelization over iterations.

This method processes a specific component configuration for a building across all wind orientations, wind speeds, and flood depths using Monte Carlo simulation with parallel processing over iterations.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default building Building

The building object to process.

required ComponentCombination ndarray

Retained for compatibility with existing caller signatures.

required cIndex int

The 1-based component configuration index to process.

required

Returns:

Name Type Description tuple tuple

A tuple containing (building.BldgType, cIndex, averaged_damage_probability_array), or None if this combination should be skipped based on user filters.

Info

When Config.EXPORT_DETAILED_DAMAGE_RATIOS is True, this method also exports detailed damage ratio breakdowns to a CSV file for each (building_type, cIndex) combination. The CSV file contains damage ratios averaged over Monte Carlo iterations for each (wind_orientation, wind_speed, flood_depth) combination.

The CSV file is saved to Config.OUTPUTS_PATH with the naming pattern: DetailedDR_m{building_type}_c{cIndex}_iter{NUM_OF_ITERATIONS}.csv

This method opens and reads a JSON file specified by path_to_file. If the JSON contains a list, it returns a numpy array of that list. docs.text:
Configure the analysis parameters and import required modules.

Key Configuration for This Demo:

  • EXPORT_DETAILED_DAMAGE_RATIOS = True: Enables export of detailed component-level damage ratios to CSV

When enabled, the following columns are exported per (building_type, cindex) combination:

  • m: Building type identifier
  • c: Component configuration index
  • wind_orientation_index: Wind orientation index
  • wind_speed_index: Wind speed index
  • flood_depth_index: Flood depth index
  • dr_total: Total building damage ratio
  • dr_explicit: Explicit damage ratio (wind components)
  • dr_implicit: Implicit damage ratio (interior + flood)
  • dr_exp_wind_RC: Roof Coverings explicit damage ratio
  • dr_exp_wind_RS: Roof Sheathings explicit damage ratio
  • dr_exp_wind_RWC: Roof-Wall Connections explicit damage ratio
  • dr_exp_wind_O: Openings explicit damage ratio
  • dr_exp_wind_W: Walls explicit damage ratio
  • dr_imp_wind_I: Interior implicit damage ratio
  • dr_imp_wind_E: Electrical implicit damage ratio
  • dr_imp_wind_M: Mechanical implicit damage ratio
  • dr_imp_wind_P: Plumbing implicit damage ratio
  • dr_imp_flood: Flood implicit damage ratio

docs.title: CHEERSafe Demo: Complete Hurricane Damage Analysis Workflow¶
docs.text: This notebook demonstrates the complete workflow for hurricane damage and loss assessment using the CHEERSafe package. We'll walk through each step from initial setup to final visualization of results.

docs.title: Prerequisites¶
docs.text:
• Python 3.12+
  • CHEERSafe package installed
  • Required input files (building geometry, etc.)

docs.title: Setup and Environment Configuration¶
docs.text: First, we'll set up the notebook environment with automatic reloading for development.

docs.title: System Configuration¶
docs.text: Let's check the available CPU cores for parallel processing configuration.

docs.title: Package Configuration and Imports¶
docs.text:
Configure the analysis parameters and import required modules. The configuration allows you to customize:

  • NUM_OF_WORKERS: Number of parallel workers for computation
  • NUM_OF_ITERATIONS: Number of Monte Carlo iterations
  • INPUTS_PATH: Directory containing input files
  • OUTPUTS_PATH: Directory for output files

docs.title: Initialize Core Components¶
docs.text:
Set up the building inventory and statistical analysis tools:

  • BuildingInventory: Manages building data and configurations
  • Covariance: Handles covariance calculations for uncertainty analysis
  • Sampling: Provides sampling methods for Monte Carlo simulation

docs.title: Create Main Analysis Engine¶
docs.text: Initialize the damage probability calculation engine with our configured components.

docs.title: Configure Analysis Parameters¶
docs.text:
Specify which building types and resistance indices to process in this analysis:

  • Building Type 2: Specific building classification
  • Resistance Index 46: Specific structural resistance category

docs.title: Run Damage Probability Analysis¶
docs.text: Execute the main damage probability calculation. This step performs Monte Carlo simulations to calculate damage probabilities under various loading conditions.

docs.title: Aggregate Results¶
docs.text: Collect and aggregate the calculated probabilities for further analysis.

docs.title: Results Analysis and Visualization¶
docs.text: Use the analysis module to visualize and interpret the calculated damage probabilities.

docs.title: Generate Analysis Plots¶
docs.text: Create comprehensive plots showing damage probability relationships and fragility curves.

docs.title: Summary¶
docs.text:
This notebook demonstrated the complete CHEERSafe workflow:

  1. Setup: Environment configuration and package imports
  2. Initialization: Building inventory and statistical tools setup
  3. Configuration: Analysis parameters and building type selection
  4. Calculation: Monte Carlo damage probability analysis
  5. Visualization: Results analysis and plotting

The generated plots show the relationship between wind speeds, structural parameters, and damage probabilities, providing insights for hurricane risk assessment and mitigation planning.

docs.title: Next Steps¶
docs.text:
• Experiment with different building types and resistance indices
  • Adjust the number of iterations for different accuracy/speed trade-offs
  • Explore the API documentation for advanced customization options

docs.title: Installation Guide for cheersafe package
docs.text: This guide will help you install the cheersafe package on your system.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
Ensure that you have Python and pip installed on your system. You can check this by running the following commands in your terminal:

python --version
pip --version

If you do not have Python or pip installed, please install them first.

docs.text:

docs.title: Step 4: Visualize Results
docs.text:
Analyze and visualize the damage probability results:

from cheersafe.damage_probability_analysis import DamageProbabilityAnalysis

# Define analysis parameters
building_type = 2
c_index = 46

# Initialize analysis with results file
myDamageProbabilityAnalysis = DamageProbabilityAnalysis(
    prob_ds_file_path="Outputs/ProbDS_wfd_dictMaxIter50_aggregated.pkl",
    building_type=building_type,
    resistance_type=c_index
)

# Generate visualization plots
myDamageProbabilityAnalysis.plot_analysis_results()
